hints: Focus on the gas first, since every carbonate releases one molecule of carbon dioxide when it reacts with excess acid.
Convert 200 cm3 of gas at room conditions into moles using 24,000 cm3 per mole, you should get about 0.00833 mol.
Use mass divided by moles to find the Mr of the carbonate, then see which metal gives a total very close to 100.
walkthrough:
**Write the carbonate reaction**

Think of it simply, carbonate plus acid always gives salt plus water plus carbon dioxide. With excess acid, all the carbonate is converted.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{MCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{MCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
For a Group 1 carbonate the balancing is slightly different, but the key ratio is still 1 mol carbonate to 1 mol $\text{CO}_2$.

**Find moles of gas released**

Under room conditions, 1 mol of any gas occupies $24.0 \text{ dm}^3$, which is $24,000 \text{ cm}^3$. So we just divide the volume by the molar volume.

Calculation:
$$n(\text{CO}_2) = \frac{200}{24,000} = 0.00833 \text{ mol}$$
This means moles of metal carbonate reacted is also $0.00833 \text{ mol}$.

**Calculate Mr and identify the metal**

Now use the golden rule, moles equals mass over Mr, rearranged to Mr equals mass over moles.

Calculation:
$$M_r = \frac{0.833}{0.00833} \approx 100$$
Subtract the $\text{CO}_3$ part ($12.0 + 3 \times 16.0 = 60.0$) to leave about 40 for the metal, which matches calcium. So the compound is $\text{CaCO}_3$.

options.A: Na2CO3 has Mr = (2 x 23.0) + 12.0 + (3 x 16.0) = 106. This would give moles = 0.833 / 106 = 0.00786 mol and only about 189 cm3 of gas, slightly less than observed.
options.B: K2CO3 has Mr = (2 x 39.1) + 12.0 + (3 x 16.0) = 138.2. This is much too heavy, so 0.833 g would give only about 0.00603 mol and about 145 cm3 of gas.
options.C: MgCO3 has Mr = 24.3 + 12.0 + (3 x 16.0) = 84.3. This is too light, so 0.833 g would give about 0.00988 mol and about 237 cm3 of gas, more than observed.
options.D: CaCO3 has Mr = 40.1 + 12.0 + (3 x 16.0) = 100.1. Moles = 0.833 / 100.1 = 0.00832 mol, giving volume = 0.00832 x 24,000 = 200 cm3, exactly matching the experiment.
